query: A Partnership Offered A shipping house in the harbour has heard about your purse, or rather about how you filled it. Its old partner wants to retire, and offers you his desk and his share of the ledger from the autumn. "Bring your crowns," he writes. "Bring your nerve. Answer on the last day." Write back that you're interested You reply on the cream paper's own back, which seems businesslike. By return comes a ledger page with a column already headed with your name. Ask to see the books first He sends them, all of them, and you find the hole in the third year that he hoped you'd find. "Good," says his next letter. "The last partner didn't."
